paraphrase: For the sake of steady knowledge, fifteen limbs are taught in order: restraint, observance, renunciation, silence, place, time, posture, the root-lock, equipoise of the body, steadiness of vision, control of breath, withdrawal, holding, meditation on the self, and samādhi — each understood as a discipline of knowledge (e.g. restraint as control of the senses by knowing 'all is Brahman').
notes: Verse numbers of the list (given as 100–101 or 102–103 in different editions) are low confidence; the fifteen limbs are certain.

original.text: dṛṣṭiṃ jñānamayīṃ kṛtvā paśyed brahmamayaṃ jagat / sā dṛṣṭiḥ paramodārā na nāsāgrāvalokinī
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: Making one's vision full of knowledge, one should see the world as Brahman; that is the noblest vision, not looking at the tip of the nose.
notes: Reinterpretation of the yogic gaze (dṛk-sthiti). Verse number moderate confidence.

original.text: ko 'haṃ katham idaṃ jātaṃ ko vai kartāsya vidyate / upādānaṃ kim astīha vicāraḥ so 'yam īdṛśaḥ
original.edition: vulgate wording recalled from memory (verify against an edition)

paraphrase: 'Who am I? How was this (world) born? Who is its maker? What is its material cause?' — such is inquiry (vicāra).
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution traditional or disputed).

paraphrase: Obstacles arise in practising samādhi: lack of inquiry, laziness, desire for enjoyment, dullness (laya), darkness, distraction, relishing (rasāsvāda) and blankness (śūnyatā); the knower of Brahman should gradually abandon them.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution traditional or disputed).

paraphrase: This rāja-yoga (of knowledge) combined with haṭha-yoga is for those whose worldly desires are not fully burnt; for those whose minds are fully ripe, this rāja-yoga alone brings perfection.
notes: Attributed to Śaṅkara (attribution traditional or disputed).
